issues.legal_issue: A standalone compound wall encroaching on public land is governed by the rule applicable to walls that are not part of a building.
material_facts: The offending structure was a compound wall encroaching on municipal roadside land.
The courts found that the wall was not part of the main building.
issues.conclusion: The offending structure fell under section 300, rather than section 299, of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1923.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 299 and 300 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1923, distinguish between structures forming part of a building and a wall that is not part of a building. The latter is dealt with under section 300.

predicates.municipal_encroachment_case: The case concerns an alleged encroachment on land under municipal control.
predicates.offending_structure_is_standalone_wall: The person accused of the encroachment erected or maintained a wall that was not part of a building.

issues.definition: When a municipal encroachment case concerns a standalone wall, the structure falls under the rule for walls outside buildings.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction may be altered to the offence established by the evidence when the alteration does not change the substance of the accusation.
material_facts: The notice and initial conviction referred to the provision applicable to a structure forming part of a building.
The courts found that the structure was a compound wall that was not part of the main building, making a different provision applicable.
The facts sought to be proved and found remained the same after the conviction was altered.
The accused was aware of the nature of the accusation.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could alter the conviction to the provision applicable to the facts found; the alteration was not illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 236 and 237 of the Code of Criminal Procedure permit a conviction for an offence established by the evidence even when the charge was framed for another offence. Relying on Begu v. The King-Emperor, the Court held that the same principle applied here because the facts remained unchanged and only the applicable section was corrected.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.evidence_establishes_different_applicabl: The evidence establishes an offence different from the one identified in the original accusation.
predicates.underlying_facts_remain_unchanged: The facts relied on to prove the accusation remain the same after the conviction is altered.

issues.definition: If a criminal appeal concerns a conviction and the evidence establishes a different applicable offence on unchanged facts, the conviction may be altered to the offence established.

issues.legal_issue: A municipal removal requisition is lawful in substance even if its heading cites the wrong provision, when its operative terms clearly identify the encroachment and require its removal.
material_facts: The notice was headed as issued under the provision for structures forming part of a building.
Its operative terms required removal of the encroachment caused by the compound wall.
The accused received the notice and did not comply with it.
The municipality was entitled to require removal of the encroachment.
issues.conclusion: The requisition was lawfully made notwithstanding the incorrect heading, and failure to comply attracted the applicable penalty.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 488(1)(c) of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1923, failure to comply with a direction lawfully given or requisition lawfully made is punishable. The substance and effective part of the notice, rather than its heading, determines whether the requisition was lawful.

predicates.prosecution_for_failure_to_comply_with_m: The proceeding prosecutes a person for failing to comply with a municipal removal requisition.
predicates.operative_notice_clearly_identifies_encr: The operative terms of the notice identify the encroachment and require the recipient to remove it.
predicates.recipient_failed_to_comply: The recipient did not carry out the removal required by the notice.

issues.definition: When a recipient in a prosecution for failure to comply with a municipal requisition receives a notice that clearly identifies the encroachment and requires its removal but does not comply, the requisition is lawful despite an incorrect heading.

issues.legal_issue: Correcting the provision underlying a conviction does not create substantial prejudice unless the accused was prejudiced in the conduct of the trial.
material_facts: The accused argued that the altered conviction caused prejudice because he might have been entitled to claim compensation under the provision originally cited.
He had himself asked the High Court to interfere with the lower courts’ conviction.
The High Court reduced the fine when it altered the conviction.
Any claim to compensation in a civil court was independent of the criminal judgment.
The accused did not show that he had been misled or deprived of an opportunity to defend himself because of the error.
issues.conclusion: The alteration caused no substantial prejudice to the accused.
issues.legal_principle: Prejudice must relate to an irregularity in the trial. A difference in the provision cited does not establish prejudice where the accused was not misled or deprived of an opportunity to make a proper defence; a possible civil claim for compensation is unaffected by the criminal judgment.

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_corrected_co: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a conviction that was corrected to cite a different applicable offence.
predicates.accused_not_misled_or_deprived_of_defenc: The accused was neither misled by the correction nor deprived of an opportunity to make a proper defence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges a corrected conviction but the accused was not misled or deprived of a defence opportunity, the correction causes no substantial prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A prosecution is not barred by limitation when the evidence establishes that the complaint was lodged within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The accused argued that the prosecution was instituted beyond the applicable limitation period.
Official documents were proved as additional evidence after the case was remanded for rehearing.
The additional evidence established that the complaint had been lodged within the prescribed period.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution was not barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 534 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1923, prescribed a limitation period for the prosecution. The additional evidence established that the complaint was lodged in time.

predicates.municipal_offence_prosecution: The proceeding prosecutes an alleged municipal offence subject to a prescribed limitation period.
predicates.evidence_establishes_complaint_was_lodge: The evidence establishes that the complaint was lodged before the applicable limitation period expired.

issues.definition: When evidence in a municipal offence prosecution establishes that the complaint was lodged within the prescribed period, the prosecution is not barred by limitation.
